title: NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor retains an unconditional tail window-restart; NatSpec 'parity with stake' is stale post-story-020
description: story-020 removed the permissionless stake/unstake tail _recomputeSchedule (closing M-01 rate-drift, fp b58b172e, fixed @321d0a9), but depositFor RETAINS an unconditional tail _recomputeSchedule (L767) that restarts windowEnd = now + windowSeconds on every call. depositFor is onlyMigrator (trusted, not permissionless) and cannot be repeatably invoked by an attacker to grief the window, so this is a faithfulness/operational residual, NOT a regression of M-01. The NatSpec claim of 'parity with stake' (L766-767) is now stale/false: stake() no longer recomputes post-story-020.
impact: None to assets (value-conserving, solvency-safe). Each owner-orchestrated migrateIn -> depositFor re-injection restarts the depletion window, deferring the horizon. Because inflow via the migrator is a genuine re-seed the behaviour is value-conserving, but it diverges from the post-story-020 stake() semantics the NatSpec still claims parity with. Low.
attackPath: 1. Owner-orchestrated migrateIn -> staker.depositFor(user, amt) runs the unconditional tail _recomputeSchedule.

2. Each re-injection restarts the depletion window, deferring the horizon; value-conserving but divergent from stake()'s post-story-020 no-recompute semantics that the NatSpec still claims parity with.
recommendation: Gate the depositFor tail recompute on inflow > 0 to mirror the story-020 stake/unstake fix (restart the window only on a real budget increase), and correct the 'parity with stake' NatSpec at L766-767 (stake no longer recomputes).
category: Low spec-deviation / stale-NatSpec residual on a trusted path (Law 2 faithfulness; no asset/availability/griefing impact)
